latest_release.name: v2.7.14
latest_release.body:
## Behavior changes: read before upgrading

### A Content-Length set through Nginx::Headers_out is no longer sent as a response header line

- Before: `Nginx::Headers_out#[]=` with the name `Content-Length` added a `Content-Length` response header line next to the one that nginx writes from the length of the response body, so a response could carry two `Content-Length` lines with different values.
- Now: a `Content-Length` that a script sets through `Nginx::Headers_out` is not sent; nginx sends its own `Content-Length` for the response, as it does when the script sets none.
- Why it changed:
  - The defect: the second `Content-Length` line that a script's value added next to the one nginx writes.
  - Why the old behavior could not be kept: the line a script set could not be made to agree with the body in every case, so the fix sends only the length that nginx frames the body by.
  - What the documentation promised: `docs/class_and_method/` on the 2.x line did not describe setting `Content-Length` through `Nginx::Headers_out`.
- Affected: a configuration whose Ruby code sets `Content-Length` through `Nginx::Headers_out` in a content handler, a phase handler or an output header filter. Reading `Content-Length` with `Nginx::Headers_out#[]` and removing it with `#delete` are unchanged.
- What to do: remove the `Nginx::Headers_out#[]=` of `Content-Length`; nginx sends the length of the response. A response of a fixed length is sent by writing that many bytes with `Nginx.rputs`, whose total nginx sends as the `Content-Length`.

---

## 更新前に確認する挙動の変更

### Nginx::Headers_outで設定したContent-Lengthを、応答のヘッダ行として送らなくなりました

- 変更前：`Nginx::Headers_out#[]=`のキーに`Content-Length`を指定すると、nginxが応答の本文の長さをもとに出力する`Content-Length`とは別に、もう1つの`Content-Length`の行が応答に追加されていました。そのため、値の異なる2つの`Content-Length`の行を持つ応答になることがありました。
- 変更後：`Nginx::Headers_out`で設定した`Content-Length`は送られなくなりました。スクリプトが設定しないときと同じく、nginx自身が応答の`Content-Length`を出力します。
- 変更の理由：
  - 不具合：`Nginx::Headers_out`で設定した`Content-Length`が、nginxが出力する行とは別に、2つ目の`Content-Length`の行として追加されていました。
  - 前の挙動を残せなかった理由：スクリプトが設定した行を、どの場合でも本文と一致させることはできないため、nginxが本文を区切るのに使う長さだけを送ります。
  - ドキュメントが示していた挙動：2.x系の`docs/class_and_method/`は、`Nginx::Headers_out`で`Content-Length`を設定する動作を説明していませんでした。
- 影響の範囲：content handler、フェーズのハンドラ、output header filterのいずれかで、Rubyのコードが`Nginx::Headers_out`を通じて`Content-Length`を設定している構成。`Nginx::Headers_out#[]`による`Content-Length`の読み取りと、`#delete`による削除は変わりません。
- 必要な対応：スクリプトから、`Content-Length`への`Nginx::Headers_out#[]=`による代入を削除してください。nginxが応答の長さを出力します。固定長の応答を返すには、その長さのバイト列を`Nginx.rputs`で出力すれば、その合計をnginxが`Content-Length`として送ります。

---

ngx_mruby: A Fast and Memory-Efficient Nginx Extension Mechanism Scripting with mruby.

## Documents - [Install](https://github.com/matsumotory/ngx_mruby/tree/master/docs/install) - [Test](https://github.com/matsumotory/ngx_mruby/tree/master/docs/test) - [Directives](https://github.com/matsumotory/ngx_mruby/tree/master/docs/directives) - [Class and Method](https://github.com/matsumotory/ngx_mruby/tree/master/docs/class_and_method) - [Use Case](https://github.com/matsumotory/ngx_mruby/tree/master/docs/use_case) - [Release notes (behaviour changes to read before upgrading)](https://github.com/matsumotory/ngx_mruby/tree/master/docs/releases) - [Trust boundary](https://github.com/matsumotory/ngx_mruby/blob/master/docs/README.md#trust-boundary): the configuration and its Ruby code are trusted, what a client sends is not, and what each side is responsible for - [Examples](https://github.com/hsbt/nginx-tech-talk) ## Branch strategy ngx_mruby has three long-lived code branches: `master`, `next` and `v2.x`. Their names and roles stay as they are. `master` is the 2.x line until v3 is promoted to it, so that everyone who builds from the default branch keeps receiving the 2.x security fixes. v3 is developed on `next` and becomes `master` at v3.0.0 (the promotion). From then on, `v2.x` carries 2.x. The site, [ngx.mruby.org](https://ngx.mruby.org/), is built from `docs/` by `.github/workflows/site.yml` on `next` and deployed by GitHub Actions: 3.x from `next` at the unprefixed paths, 2.x from `master` under `/v2/`. The `gh-pages` branch keeps the old site as history. ```text until the promotion | after the promotion | next ---*alpha.1---*beta.1---*rc.1---*rc.N---+ | - - ? \ master -*v2.7.0--*v2.7.x-- ... -----------o------M------*------*--- ... --> 3.x : : : v2.x -*v2.7.0--*v2.7.x-- ... -----------o----------*------*------ ... --] 2.x * a release tag (v2.*, v3.*) or a pre-release tag (v3.0.0-*); v2.7.x stands for the 2.x releases after v2.7.0 o the last 2.x commit on master : the same commit on both branches M the merge of next into master, tagged v3.0.0 ? what next becomes after the promotion is open (see the table below) ] the end of 2.x support, twelve months after v3.0.0 The merges of master into next before the promotion are not drawn. ``` | Branch | Until the promotion | After the promotion (v3.0.0) | |---|---|---| | `master` (default branch) | The 2.x line: 2.x fixes, `v2.*` releases | The 3.x line: `v3.*` releases | | `v2.x` | The same commits as `master`: a workflow copies every push to `master` to `v2.x` | The 2.x line: stability and security fixes, `v2.*` releases | | `next` | Development of v3 and its pre-releases | Open; the recommendation is to keep it for the development of 3.1 (see [Promoting v3 to master](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#promoting-v3-to-master)) | Until the promotion, `master` is merged into `next` after 2.x fixes, so v3 has them too. v3 is developed on `next`. Its pre-releases are tagged `v3.0.0-alpha.N`, `v3.0.0-beta.N` and `v3.0.0-rc.N` and are marked as pre-releases on GitHub. Section 6 of the v3 plan ([docs/proposals/v3-plan.md](https://github.com/matsumotory/ngx_mruby/blob/next/docs/proposals/v3-plan.md) on `next`) sets when the first pre-release of each kind is tagged: - `v3.0.0-alpha.1`: when the 2.x test suite passes on the new core of v3 and the sanitizers report nothing. - `v3.0.0-beta.1`: when the migration guide and the examples exist. - `v3.0.0-rc.1`: when the site and the examples are complete. `v3.0.0` is tagged when `next` is promoted to `master`, under the conditions in [Promoting v3 to master](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#promoting-v3-to-master). No date is set. At least one `v3.0.0-rc.N` comes first, and how long the last one stays out before v3.0.0 is still open. The pre-releases and releases appear on the [releases page](https://github.com/matsumotory/ngx_mruby/releases); to be notified of them, watch the repository with "Custom" and "Releases" selected. ### For existing users If you do not want anything to change, build from `v2.x` or from the latest `v2.*` release tag instead of `master`, and switch now: ```sh git clone -b v2.x https://github.com/matsumotory/ngx_mruby.git # the 2.x branch git clone -b vX.Y.Z https://github.com/matsumotory/ngx_mruby.git # or the latest v2.* release tag ``` A release tag does not receive fixes. If you pin one, move to each new 2.x release, because only the latest 2.x release is supported (see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md#supported-versions)), or pin `v2.x`, which receives the 2.x fixes as they are merged. If you start using ngx_mruby now, the same applies: for production, build from `v2.x` or the latest `v2.*` release tag, and to try v3, track `next`. Until the promotion, `v2.x` has the same commits as `master`, so pinning it does not change the code you build until then. At the promotion, `master` becomes v3.0.0, a new major version. Section 7 of the [v3 plan](https://github.com/matsumotory/ngx_mruby/blob/next/docs/proposals/v3-plan.md) already decides changes to its build requirements and behavior: mruby 4.1 instead of 3.3; nginx 1.30 (stable) and 1.31 (mainline) as the oldest supported versions, raised every April, so that users of older nginx stay on 2.x (2.x builds with nginx 1.28 and 1.26, and with nginx 1.24, which Linux distributions package, only without stream, that is, without `--with-stream`); OpenSSL 3.5 as the baseline with 1.1.1 and 3.0 dropped; `auto-ssl` removed from the default build; and the behavior changes of item 8: a Ruby API called outside the phase it is designed for raises an exception, an exception after `rputs` returns 500, `Headers#delete` matches the full header name, `Nginx.return 200` with an empty body is allowed, and a body is sent with any status. The [v3 migration guide](https://github.com/matsumotory/ngx_mruby/blob/next/docs/migration/README.md) on `next` lists each of these changes once it is merged there. The 2.x line (`master` until the promotion, then `v2.x`) puts compatibility first. It receives only stability fixes (crashes, hangs, leaks, and build fixes such as those for new nginx, OS, compiler or OpenSSL releases) and security fixes, and it changes behavior only as far as the fix of a defect requires. Since 2.7.1, the release notes in [docs/releases/](docs/releases/) list each such change. 2.x stays supported for twelve months after v3.0.0 (see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md#supported-versions)). Releases are tagged `vX.Y.Z`. If you contribute a fix, send 2.x fixes to `master` until the promotion and v3 work to `next` (see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#branches-and-pull-requests)). Before upgrading, read the "Behavior changes: read before upgrading" section of every newer release in [docs/releases/](docs/releases/). Please report security vulnerabilities privately as described in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). The project has earned the passing level of the [OpenSSF Best Practices badge](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/16057). ## What's ngx_mruby __ngx_mruby is A Fast and Memory-Efficient TCP/UDP Load Balancing and Web Server Extension Mechanism Using Scripting Language mruby for nginx.__ - ngx_mruby is to provide an alternative to lua-nginx-module or [mod_mruby of Apache httpd](http://mod.mruby.org/). - Unified Ruby Code between Apache(mod_mruby), nginx(ngx_mruby) and other Web server software(plan) for Web server extensions. - You can implement nginx modules by Ruby scripts on nginx! - You can implement some Web server software extensions by same Ruby code (as possible) - Supported nginx main-line and stable-line (the stream module needs nginx 1.25.5 or later; see [Building with ngx_mruby stream module](docs/install/README.md#building-with-ngx_mruby-stream-module)) - [Benchmark between ngx_mruby and lua-nginx-module](https://www.techempower.com/benchmarks/#section=data-r10&hw=peak&test=plaintext&w=4-0) ```ruby # location /proxy { # mruby_set $backend "/path/to/proxy.rb"; # proxy_pass http://$backend; # } backends = [ "test1", "test2", "test3", ] r = Redis.new "192.168.12.251", 6379 r.get backends[rand(backends.length)] ``` This example needs the `Redis` class of mruby-redis, and a running Redis server. The default `build_config.rb` builds mruby-redis again since 2.7.2; 2.7.1 left it out. - see [examples](https://github.com/matsumotory/ngx_mruby/blob/master/example/nginx.conf) - __Sample of Unified Ruby Code between Apache(mod_mruby) and nginx(ngx_mruby) for Web server extensions__ - You can implement some Web server software extensions by same Ruby code (as possible) ```ruby # Unified Ruby Code between Apache(mod_mruby) and nginx(ngx_mruby) # for Web server extensions. # # Apache httpd.conf by mod_mruby # # # mrubyHandlerMiddle "/path/to/unified_hello.rb" # # # nginx nginx.conf by ngx_mruby # # location /mruby { # mruby_content_handler "/path/to/unified_hello.rb"; # } # Server = get_server_class Server::rputs "Hello #{Server::module_name}/#{Server::module_version} world!" # mod_mruby => "Hello mod_mruby/0.9.3 world!" # ngx_mruby => "Hello ngx_mruby/0.0.1 world!" ``` [![ngx_mruby mod_mruby performance](https://github.com/matsumotory/mod_mruby/raw/master/images/performance_20140301.png)](http://blog.matsumoto-r.jp/?p=3974) ※ [hello world simple benchmark, see details of blog entry.](http://blog.matsumoto-r.jp/?p=3974) ## Abstract As the increase of large-scale and complex Web services, not only the development of Web applications is required, but also the implementation of Web server extensions in many cases. Most Web server extensions are mainly implemented in the C language because of fast and memory-efficient behavior, but by writing extensions using a scripting language we can achieve better maintainability and productivity. However, if the existing methods are primarily intended to enhance not the implementation of Web applications but the implementation of internal processing of the Web server, the problem remains in terms of speed, memory-efficiency and safety. Therefore, we propose a fast and memory-efficient Web server extension mechanism using a scripting language. We designed an architecture where the server process creates a region in memory to save the state of the interpreter at the server process startup, and multiple scripts share this region to process the scripts quickly when new request are made. The server process frees the global variables table, the exception flag and the byte-code which cause an increase of memory usage, in order to reduce the memory usage and extend safety by preventing interference between each script because of sharing the region. We implemented a mechanism that can extend the internal processing of nginx easily by Ruby scripts using nginx and the embeddable scripting language mruby. It's called "ngx_mruby". ### What a worker keeps between requests The abstract above describes the design of the paper. ngx_mruby today does not free the global variables table between scripts. nginx creates one `mrb_state` for the `http {}` block (and one for the `stream {}` block) while it reads the configuration, and runs the init code (`mruby_init`, `mruby_stream_init`) and the server configuration code (`mruby_server_context_handler_code`) in it before it starts the workers, in the master process. Each worker process gets its own copy when nginx forks it, and runs all the other mruby code of the block in that copy: the init_worker and exit_worker code and every handler and filter, in every server and location, for every client. A reload or a restart starts new workers with a new state. Global variables, constants, instance variables of `main` (the `self` of handler code), methods defined with `def`, classes and modules with their constants, and what `Userdata` holds (it keeps its values in a global variable) stay in the worker from one request to the next. What one request leaves behind is seen by every later request that the same worker handles, also when the code raised an exception after it made the change. Each worker has its own copy, so one worker does not see the values of another. After each run, ngx_mruby clears the exception (`mrb->exc`); a script file without `cache` is read and compiled again for the next run, and inline code and cached scripts keep the byte-code compiled at startup. The garbage collector frees the objects that nothing refers to any more. Local variables do not stay: each run of handler code starts without them. Do not keep the data of one request in global variables, constants, instance variables of `main` or `Userdata`, since the next request of the worker, from any client, sees it. Use local variables, and read and write the request through `Nginx::Request`, `Nginx::Var`, `Nginx::Headers_in` and `Nginx::Headers_out` (in `stream {}`, where code runs per session, `Nginx::Stream::Connection`). To pass data from one handler to a later handler of the same request, declare an nginx variable with `set $name "";` and read and write it through `Nginx::Var`, or set the `Userdata` value in every request before it is read. A `set` in the location runs after `mruby_rewrite_handler` and empties the variable again, so declare a variable that a rewrite handler writes with `set` in the `server {}` block. Keep in globals and constants only what all requests of the worker are meant to share, such as settings that the init or init_worker code prepares. [`Nginx.remove_global_variable`](docs/class_and_method/README.md#nginxremove_global_variable) removes a global variable. # Contributions This project exists thanks to all the people who contribute.
